Anisha Kinnarath Salam is gearing up for an important week.

AK Soccer Academy, the Winnipeg-based club Kinnarath Salam and her father started in 2019, is in Surrey, B.C., this week for the Canada Soccer National Championships — a first for the 15U girls team — and Kinnarath Salam believes her side has a legitimate shot at winning it all.

“We’ve had the squad, but this is a very talented group,” said Kinnarath Salam. “A few of these girls have been with us since they were five years old. A few have been with us since they were like 10. But we got some powerhouses last year.”

SUPPLIED

Dual athlete Quinn Lavoie has broken records on the track and has been named as a reserve player for the U16 national soccer team.

One of those new headlining talents is winger Quinn Lavoie, a product of West St. Paul who has brought a tantalizing blend of speed, technical skill and high IQ on the pitch.

Lavoie helped lead AK Soccer Academy to a 19-1-1 record in the Winnipeg Youth Soccer Association and win the Manitoba Soccer Association Cup, punching the club’s ticket to the national tournament. AK went 4-1 in provincials — their only loss coming without Lavoie in the lineup — and won the championship final 7-2 after receiving four goals from Lavoie.

“My dad calls her Batman because her presence on the team is very uplifting, and there’s a lot of comfort from her teammates when she’s on the team and when she’s on the pitch because they know that she’s going to lead on the pitch and lead by example,” said Kinnarath Salam.

“When you have your best player on the field, but she brings out the best of everyone, and then she elevates also players around her, we have a very strong group, and it takes a lot of pressure off of our other star players when she’s around, and vice versa. It’s a good group, and they’re very well balanced and gelled.”

Lavoie is doing more than scoring goals, however.
